# Date

A calendar date that exists.

```rux
pub struct Date {
    pub year: int32;
    pub month: uint8;
    pub day: uint8;
}
```

`Copy`. Only constructible through the fallible [`New`](/docs/api/time/date#new) factory, which lets everything downstream assume validity.

## Fields

| Name    | Type    | Description                                                    |
| ------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `year`  | `int32` | The year, astronomically numbered: year 0 exists and is 1 BCE. |
| `month` | `uint8` | The month, 1 through 12.                                       |
| `day`   | `uint8` | The day, 1 through the month's length.                         |

<h3 id="from-epoch-days"><code>FromEpochDays</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FromEpochDays(days: int64) -> Date
```

The date `days` after 1970-01-01, negative before it.
The inverse of [`DaysFromEpoch`](/docs/api/time/date#days-from-epoch), exactly: the pair round-trips every day of every representable year.

| Name   | Type    | Description   |
| ------ | ------- | ------------- |
| `days` | `int64` | how many days |

**Returns**: the date that many days after 1970-01-01

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L81)

## Methods

<h3 id="days-from-epoch"><code>DaysFromEpoch</code></h3>

```rux
pub func DaysFromEpoch(self: &Date) -> int64
```

Days since 1970-01-01, negative before it.
The civil-calendar formula: the year is shifted so March opens it, which puts the leap day at the end where
it cannot disturb the month arithmetic.

**Returns**: days since 1970-01-01, negative before it

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L63)

<h3 id="plus-days"><code>PlusDays</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PlusDays(self: &Date, days: int64) -> Date?
```

The date `days` later, negative for earlier, or `None` outside the years the calendar spells.
Exact: a day is a day, and the round trip through the epoch count neither loses nor invents one.

| Name   | Type    | Description   |
| ------ | ------- | ------------- |
| `days` | `int64` | how many days |

**Returns**: the date that many days later, or `None` when it leaves the range

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L19)

<h3 id="plus-months"><code>PlusMonths</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PlusMonths(self: &Date, months: int64) -> Date?
```

The date `months` later, clamped to the month's end where the day is missing.
January 31st plus one month is the last day of February; the clamp is the policy the module header states.

| Name     | Type    | Description     |
| -------- | ------- | --------------- |
| `months` | `int64` | how many months |

**Returns**: the date that many months later, clamped to the month's last day, or `None` when it leaves the range

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L33)

## Implements Display

`Date` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(self: &Date, writer: &var TextWriter, spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
A year outside 0 through 9999 carries a sign and as many digits as it needs, which is what ISO 8601 requires
for one: four digits is the agreed width, and anything wider is ambiguous without a sign to mark it.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than `iso8601` or
`rfc3339`, or for a precision, which a date has nothing to apply one to.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole date was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L154)

<h3 id="parse-date"><code>ParseDate</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseDate(text: char8[..]) -> Date ! TimeParseError
```

Reads `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Strict: four year digits, two month digits, two day digits, dashes between, and nothing after.
Reports `InvalidSyntax` for a shape that does not match, `InvalidMonth` for a month outside 1 through 12, and
`NonexistentDay` for a day the month does not have. Each carries the byte offset where it was found.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/CalendarParse.rux#L233)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description      |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the date, or why the text is not one
